title: Predictive Autoscaler and Tenancy Shielding — Dedicated Capacity PRD (sketch)
content:
Context:
Small sketch for a dedicated-capacity feature that combines predictive autoscaling, temporal bursting with credit-based budget, and tenancy shielding (isolation controls). Goal is a pragmatic feature that: reduces missed SLAs during traffic spikes, keeps unit-cost predictable, and gives orgs control over noisy neighbors without manual sharding.

Why now:
- Customers on Dedicated want fewer incidents from sudden traffic bursts (webhooks, batch jobs).
- Manual reserve + manual burst is operationally expensive for customers and Redwood support.
- Existing soft-reserve logic works, but is reactive and costly under tail spikes.

High-level proposal:
1) Predictive Autoscaler: server-side controller that consumes per-tenant historical traffic series and recent signals (queue depth, request rate, token-per-request distributions) to forecast demand 1–30 minutes out and pre-warm capacity (start VMs/GPU pods, allocate slots).
   - Fast-path (0–60s): short-lived burst workers (thin pods) for low-latency bursts using pre-warmed cache/KV; priced slightly higher.
   - Warm-path (1–5m): spin up full inference instances, attach to tenant slot pool.

2) Temporal Bursting with Credits: each tenant gets a configurable burst budget (tokens and/or VM-minutes) on top of reserved capacity. Bursts draw down credits; credits refill on a schedule (daily/hourly) or via purchase. Controls: max concurrent burst nodes, per-minute token cap on burst.

3) Tenancy Shielding (Isolation Controls): policy layer that allows customers to define isolation levels per workload or route: 
   - public-shared (default): best-effort sharing with other tenants; lowest cost.
   - soft-isolated: preferred placement on tenant-affine pools; additional compute reserved per-tenant; faster throttling for other tenants when contention occurs.
   - hard-isolated: tenant-dedicated slices (no noisy neighbors), stronger SLO guarantees, higher price.
   Policies include preemption behavior, eviction windows, and fallback chains (e.g., downgrade to a cheaper model or hosted fallback).

Config model (sketch):
- reserve: {"gpu_slots": "int", "min_instances": "int"}  <-- user-friendly console fields (we will expose as typed fields in UI; below is conceptual)
- burst: {"credit_type": "tokens|minutes", "initial_credits": "number", "recharge_rate": "number per hour", "max_concurrency": "int"}
- autoscaler: {"enable_predictive": "bool", "horizon_minutes": "int", "sensitivity": "low|med|high", "slo_target_ms": "int"}
- isolation: {"level": "shared|soft|hard", "preempt_policy": "evict-oldest|stall|fallback-model"}

UX/Console ideas (quick notes):
- Quick start wizard for Dedicated customers: choose baseline reserve -> pick burst bundle -> set isolation level. Show cost delta and risk (probability of SLO miss).
- Observability: time series for forecast vs actual, credit burn rate, pre-warm events, and queue depth heatmap.
- Alerts: credit low, predictive-scaler failed to provision, and isolation-policy evictions.

APIs and primitives (ops API sketches):
- POST /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/scaling-policy  (body includes autoscaler config, burst config, isolation level)
- GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/forecast  (returns recent forecasts, state)
- GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/credits
- Admin: /v1/internal/prefetch/tenant/{id}?horizon=120

Operational details / Implementation notes (engineering callouts):
- Forecasting model: start with weighted rolling-window + seasonality + simple anomaly detection. Plan for iterative improvement to an LSTM/TS-ensembling if needed. Keep models per-tenant bucket (not per tenant at first) to control training cost.
- Safety: enforce hard rate-limits and SLO-aware throttling to avoid cascading cost overruns.
- Fast-path workers should share a small warm process image to reduce cold start; preloaded tokenizers and KV cache.
- Placement: leverage tenancy-affinity labels in scheduler; soft-isolation is preferential scheduling, hard-isolation uses explicit node pools.
- Billing: clearly separate burst usage from reserved capacity. Credits should appear in billing exports and APIs.

Metrics / Success criteria:
- Reduce SLO miss rate for spikes (>2x baseline) by 60% for customers using predictive autoscaler in pilot.
- Limit burst cost delta to <25% over baseline for typical 95th percentile spikes.
- Time-to-warm (from forecast trigger to full instance serving) median <90s.
- Fewer manual support incidents due to capacity (target: -40% supporting tickets in Q1 post-launch).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experimentation): internal feature flag; run predictive autoscaler on synthetic traffic and a couple volunteered customers (Q1).
- Phase 1 (pilot): opt-in tenancy for up to 20 customers; expose credits UI and basic isolation controls; monitor cost + reliability (Q2).
- Phase 2 (general availability): public docs, pricing bundles, autoscaler defaults, and managed pilots for large accounts (Q3).

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Chargeback model: should credits be free initially for pilot or purchasable from day 1? Pilot probably free.
- Forecast errors: how aggressive can we be without creating runaway costs? Need a kill-switch and per-tenant budget caps.
- Pre-warm churn: starting/stopping GPUs on cloud provider may be unreliable; need graceful backoff and warm pool sizing strategy.
- Complexity for customers: too many knobs can be confusing; need strong defaults and templates.

Related work + references:
- existing soft-reserve primitives (ref internal doc DOC-1372)
- backlog item: JIRA-3912 (isolation labels + scheduler integration)

Immediate next steps (for this doc):
- Align with infra for node-pool APIs and costs (owner: Marco)
- Product -> pricing to propose credit bundles (owner: Sofia)
- Engineering spike: prototype forecasting pipeline and a small warm-pool controller (owner: Daniel)
- Draft a short pilot runbook and SLOs doc for customer success (owner: Aisha)

Notes / scratchpad (informal):
- thinking: burst credits could be a hybrid token (tokens convert to VM-minutes based on a moving-price estimate)
- consider 'route-level' isolation: allow customers to mark specific API routes as hard-isolated (e.g., payments webhook)
- could integrate with Redwood Optimize to suggest sensible reserve/burst mix based on historical cost per token

End of sketch — want to keep this lightweight. Prefer follow-up sync to lock down API surface and minimal MVP for pilot.
